channel.title: Carat Capital — The Trade Paper of the Jewelry World
channel.description: Prices, intelligence and analysis from every desk of the stone trade: diamonds, gold and metals, gemstones, watches, auctions, retail and technology.

item.title: Sarine's revenue fell 6%. Its loss grew 21 times.
item.description: Sarine Technologies took $14.4 million in the first half against a net loss of $3.5 million, where a year earlier the loss was $166,000. Revenue fell about $0.9 million. The deficit widened by $3.3 million.

item.title: Three sessions of silver's gain undone in one
item.description: Gold reads $4,384.10 and silver $64.52 on this paper's tape this morning. The gold-to-silver ratio widened to 67.95 from 66.59, giving back 1.36 of the 1.82 points silver had taken out of gold across four sessions.

item.title: Titan's jewellery arm grew 43% and says diamond prices settled
item.description: Titan's jewellery division took Rs 18,253 crore in the June quarter, up 43% excluding bullion and digital gold. Its managing director says the natural-diamond market has stabilised and the lab-grown argument has quietened.

item.title: The half-carat is priced like 1999, says Kiran Gems
item.description: Senil Lakhani, president of Kiran Gems USA, says stones from 0.30 to 0.70 carats are selling at 1990s and early-2000s prices, in the $1,000 to $5,000 band that carries the American counter.

item.title: Lucara's price a carat rose 24% as its prices fell
item.description: Lucara sold 58,553 carats in the second quarter against 77,167 a year earlier and took $41.0 million against $43.7 million. That is 24% fewer stones for 6% less money, and the company says both its sales channels quoted lower prices.

item.title: 66.59: silver takes a fourth session out of gold
item.description: Gold reads $4,415.20 and silver $66.30 on this paper's tape this morning. The ratio between them has fallen on four consecutive sessions, from 68.41 to 66.59. Platinum was not written back, and the reason is printed below.

item.title: Signet gives Zales and Banter to a Mattel executive
item.description: Jamie Cygielman becomes president of Zales and Banter on 24 August, reporting to chief executive J.K. Symancyk. She arrives from Mattel, where she was global head of dolls, having earlier run American Girl.

item.title: 1.7% in the cheap colours: what July's flat month hid
item.description: This paper led on 4 August with the one-carat index flat in July, ending a thirteen-month slide. Rapaport's August newsletter breaks that flat month open by colour: K to M goods averaged 1.7% while the better colours averaged 0.1%.

item.title: $711, $650, $511: one lab-grown carat, three prices
item.description: CaratRadar's 1-carat lab-grown average read $711 on 11 August. TheDiamondPrice puts fair market at $650 inside a $590 to $760 range. This paper carried $511 from a third page on 7 August.

item.title: AED 10.44 between two Dubai gold pages, and holding
item.description: Peg arithmetic on Kitco's 06:00 spot puts Dubai 24-carat gold at AED 516.31 a gram. LivePriceOfGold reads 516.26 and Goodreturns 526.75. Both pages moved with the metal today; the distance between them did not.

item.title: Kalyan builds a second brand for one Indian state
item.description: Kalyan Jewellers opens Akshaya Thanga Maligai at Panagal Park in Chennai on 21 August, a Tamil Nadu-only banner it intends to expand by franchise. The group already runs more than 400 showrooms across seven countries.

item.title: Two Dubai gold rates, 2% apart. Neither one is wrong
item.description: Two widely quoted Dubai gold pages read AED 512.45 and AED 523.25 a gram for 24-carat this morning, a gap of AED 10.80 or 2.11%. One is publishing the metal, the other the counter.

item.title: 5.9 million pieces: India's silver rush reaches the assay office
item.description: Hallmarked silver articles in India nearly doubled to 5.9 million in the 2025-26 financial year from 3.2 million. About 230 centres handle the testing, and the standards bureau says its own labs cover roughly two more years.

item.title: Etsy cuts 12% of staff, and calls it speed
item.description: Etsy is cutting about 220 jobs, roughly 12% of the marketplace workforce, at a $35 million charge, leaving about 1,600 staff. It announced the cut alongside revenue up 6.2% to $668.3 million.

item.title: $5 billion of debt, gone in 113 days: QVC exits
item.description: QVC Group left Chapter 11 on 7 August, 113 days after filing, having cut more than $5 billion of debt. It issued $1.2 billion of 10% notes due 2032 and secured a $600 million facility.

item.title: Pandora's third seat in a year comes from Walmart
item.description: Paulo Garcia joins Pandora on 1 October and becomes chief financial officer on 1 December, succeeding Anders Boyer after more than 14 years. He arrives from Walmart's $50 billion Mexican and Central American business.

item.title: Five times its metal: a Garrard egg makes £123,500
item.description: A 22-carat gold Cadbury 'Conundrum' egg by Garrard sold for £123,500, about $166,600, at Batemans on 1 August. That is close to six times its estimate and roughly five times the melt value of its nine ounces of gold.

item.title: 640,000 ounces: China's biggest gold month since 2023
item.description: The People's Bank of China added 640,000 troy ounces in July, about 19.9 tonnes and the largest single month since October 2023. Holdings reached 76.08 million ounces, roughly 2,366 tonnes, in a 21st consecutive month of buying.

item.title: 938 at the exchange, 1,286 at the counter
item.description: Shanghai Gold Exchange Au99.99 traded at 938 yuan a gram on 8 August, up 7.53 on the day. Chow Tai Fook's 24-carat counter read 1,286 yuan, a spread of 348 yuan a gram, about 37% over the benchmark.

item.title: Turkey +6.9%, America −14.8%: where Swiss watches went
item.description: Swiss watch exports to Turkey rose 6.9% to 165.2 million francs in the first half. Shipments to the United States fell 14.8%, Germany 10.5% and China 5.0%. India rose 31.5% and Mexico 14.9%.

item.title: 46% of Kalyan's revenue came back through the door
item.description: Kalyan Jewellers took ₹10,589 crore of revenue in the June quarter, up 46%, and net profit of ₹349 crore, up 32%. Recycled gold supplied more than 46% of revenue and more than 55% in June alone.

item.title: P.N. Gadgil retires Litestyle and bets on 100 YOOU stores
item.description: P N Gadgil Jewellers replaced its lightweight diamond line Litestyle with a new brand, YOOU, on 8 August. It runs 13 exclusive outlets and shop-in-shop counters across five states, against a target of 100 stores by 2030.

item.title: The 106,000 jobs that weren't: payrolls miss puts gold at $4,341.30
item.description: July payrolls fell 23,000 against a consensus of about 83,000, a miss of 106,000. Gold closed Friday at $4,341.30, up $102.00 or 2.41%. September hike odds fell to 46% from 55% on the print.

item.title: Gold kept $26.80, platinum gave back $29.00: the settle against the spike
item.description: This paper marked all four metals at 5:58am on Friday. By the 5:00pm close gold had added a further $26.80, while platinum gave back $29.00, palladium $25.00 and silver $0.83. Only gold improved on its morning mark.

item.title: $13,000 for costume, £2,000 for gold: Bonhams runs Chanel in three cities
item.description: Bonhams will hold three Chanel sales in September: New York 7 to 17, Paris 14 to 24 with about 400 lots, London 21 September to 1 October. The top jewellery lot is a 1960 Goossens bangle at $13,000 to $20,000.

item.title: 29% said diamond, 57% said fashion jewellery: Hong Kong's two answers
item.description: HKTDC surveyed 1,507 buyers and exhibitors at its twin Hong Kong shows, 29 July to 2 August. Diamond led demand at 29%, ruby 25%, pearl 20%. Trendy fashion jewellery led growth potential at 57%, precious jewellery 35%.

item.title: Up 8.6% in dollars, down in units: the $1,500 line splits the counter
item.description: Tenoris data puts US jewellery sales up 8.6% in the first half on a 19% rise in average purchase price and a fall in units. Sales below $1,500 kept declining. June sales rose 13% year on year.

item.title: Buyers up 5%, 96% already rebooked: Rockview's first NY Now
item.description: NY Now's summer edition ran 2 to 4 August at the Javits Center with 460 exhibitors, the first under Rockview Management Group. Buyer attendance rose 5% and 96% of exhibitors have renewed for the 31 January winter show.

item.title: Fifteen years, no tax: what Mumbai just offered to take from Dubai
item.description: India's lower house passed a Bill on 6 August exempting qualifying foreign rough sellers from income tax between 1 October 2026 and 31 March 2041. It replaces a safe harbour that presumes profit at 1.25% of gross revenue, against corporate rates reaching about 33%.

item.title: $4,314.50 and silver up 4.71%: every metal runs before payrolls
item.description: At 5:58am New York gold bid $4,314.50, up $75.20 or 1.77%. Silver added $2.89 or 4.71% to $64.29, platinum 3.14% to $1,772.00 and palladium 2.14% to $1,382.00. The ratio tightened to 67.1 from 69.3. Payrolls land at 8:30am.
